notes: **2026-09-01** — (branch `fix/F10-reopen-stop-state-guards`, off master `df1ef9a3`; no schema change) — **F10 REOPENSTOP AND STOP-STATE GUARDS (B54/B55/B71/B72/B120/B121).** One seam: the delivery stop/run state machine mutated money-, stock- and compliance-bearing state without guarding WHERE a transition came from or WHO made it. **B54 —** reopen's payment guard queried the legacy `transaction` model, which has **no writer anywhere in `apps/api/src`** (the live at-door writer is `InvoicePayment` via `recordDeliveryPaymentInTx`), so it always found zero rows and always passed: a paid delivery reopened freely, leaving a PAID invoice standing against an order the system then called undelivered, and the re-collection went unrecorded because `PAYABLE` excludes PAID. `reopenStop` now also reads `invoice.findFirst({orderId: {in: orderIds}, OR: [status in PAID/PARTIAL, payments: {some: CONFIRMED_PAYMENT}]})` and 400s **before the transaction opens**; the legacy guard **STAYS** so historical rows still block. Predicate is the shared `invoices/payment-predicates` const, never a literal (F03/F05 rule). **B55 —** the "compensating positive-qty SALE" loop was a **double-credit, not a reversal**: delivery writes no stock (`currentStock` is settled at order creation and re-settled only on item edit), so it inflated stock on every reopen and minted uncosted positive SALE rows into COGS. Deleted outright with nothing in its place; the conservation rule is now uniform — **creation decrements with no movement row, delivery writes nothing, reopen writes nothing.** ⚠️ Pre-fix damage is enumerable ONLY via those rows (`type:SALE`, `quantity>0`, `reference LIKE 'Reopen stop %'`), so that reference prefix is load-bearing for the D4 repair flight — never reuse it for a new writer. **B71 —** `updateStopStatus` had **no from-state guard at all**, so a COMPLETED stop could be PATCHed straight to SKIPPED, defeating `orders.service.ts`'s demotion guard (which keys on `stop.status === "COMPLETED"`) and stranding every side effect. Now 409s on a COMPLETED stop and under a COMPLETED/CANCELLED run, and loads the run for **every** caller (was driver-only). **B72 —** new `forbiddenRunTransition(from,to)` in `dto/update-run-status.dto.ts` is a deliberate **deny-list, not a whitelist**: only CANCELLED→COMPLETED and COMPLETED→SCHEDULED are refused; same→same stays legal for idempotent retries. **CANCELLED is deliberately NOT absorbing** (narrowed in review): with `deleteRun` refusing any run that recorded a delivery, `reopenStop` refusing cancelled runs, and the dispatch sweep requiring `routeRunStopId: null` (nothing clears it on cancel — F11's), a terminal CANCELLED would strand the run and its undelivered orders permanently, so CANCELLED→SCHEDULED/IN_PROGRESS stays legal as the recovery path; drivers are refused it in `updateRunStatus` ("ask your operator to restart it"), keeping the un-cancel an operator decision. Censused the callers first — web sends only CANCELLED, mobile sends IN_PROGRESS/COMPLETED, and an operator SCHEDULED→COMPLETED backfill is spec-pinned — a whitelist would have broken all three; COMPLETED→IN_PROGRESS is allowed **deliberately**. Ownership: DRIVER callers must match `run.driverId` in `updateRunStatus`, `completeStop` **and** `completeWithPayment` (the latter two fetched the driver row and never compared it), checked before POD ingest and before the tx opens so a hijacker's capture is never stored. **B120 —** reopen nulled `signatureUrl`/`podPhotoUrls` — the only pointers to real stored objects since #477 — with no deletion anywhere, orphaning regulated-delivery evidence irrecoverably. It now writes an `AuditLog` row (`action: "route_stop.reopened"`) carrying the discarded capture **inside the same transaction**, so evidence stays recoverable and objects stay referenced; storage is deliberately NOT deleted, and that row doubles as the forward reopen trail the pre-fix era never had. The stop reset in the same tx also appends `{archivedAt, signatureUrl, podPhotoUrls, reason:"reopen"}` to `RouteRunStop.podHistory`, the column F01 added for this write (audit row = who/when; `podHistory` = the stop-local archive a read surface joins to) — nothing is appended when a reopen displaces no pointers. **B121 —** `attachPodArtifact` took **no user parameter at all** and overwrote `signatureUrl` unconditionally for any new artifactId, letting any in-tenant caller substitute a completed regulated stop's compliance signature months later. Now takes `user: JwtPayload` (controller passes `@CurrentUser`), applies the driver-run binding **before** the idempotent read, and 409s a `kind:"signature"` write on a COMPLETED stop that already has one; photos stay appendable and the same-artifactId offline replay still returns the stored artifact. The sibling READ `getStopPod` (`GET .../pod`) gained the same `user` binding in the same pass — it presigns the signature and every POD photo, and `RouteRun.driverId` is mutable via `updateRun`, so leaving the read unbound would have let a reassigned driver keep pulling the compliance evidence the write guard had just closed. **NOT F10's:** the CANCEL path and `deleteRun` settlement gates remain F11's. || History in CHANGELOG.md (this directory).
